revisions.data_semantics_impact: none for a database with no normalized duplicate words, which includes the live one: the added code is a single read-only SELECT that returns immediately. For a database that does collide, the applied version failed inside _ensure_user_word_state on UNIQUE(user_id, lexicon_entry_id) after its DDL and part of its data writes, while the current version aborts with zero changes made.
revisions.notes: THE ONE REVISION THAT CHANGED AFTER IT WAS APPLIED. Applied as blob 72348b9be6f3bdee7d8026ab97b6d3ea6caa7813 at commit 6ad8fce, later changed by cfbabc6 to blob 5d82e5dc4a08291d10e418532b61efdc16376e49. The diff is PURELY ADDITIVE: +63 lines, 0 deletions (git diff --numstat reports 63 0). The applied version had NO duplicate-word preflight at all -- the names preflight_normalized_words, find_normalized_duplicates and _normalized_word_key do not occur in it. The change adds those three read-only functions plus one call as the first statement of upgrade(), before _add_compat_columns() and _create_lexicon_tables(). No DDL, no data statement and no column definition was touched. ERRATUM: the commit message of cfbabc6 and the previous round's report describe this as moving an existing preflight; that is wrong, and this manifest is authoritative. Verified by replaying the applied version against the verified V1.1 source: the resulting revision, schema, foreign keys, indexes and content rows match the live database.
